title: P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison, Part II: generic crystalline monodromy
summary: This direction connects generic filtrations of crystalline G-objects to large p-adic Galois images. Starting from the shared period and admissibility theories, it uses decent Frobenius fibres, coefficient lines and corrected highest-weight averages to force the connected monodromy group to contain the derived group. Infinite transcendence produces the required finite-extension period points. Compact torsor components and a separately supplied quasisplit converse form the final applications.
readme: Generic crystalline monodromy extends the rational p-adic Hodge interfaces, without rebuilding period rings, neutral Tannaka, generic flag filtrations or local shtuka spaces. The reader document research/blueprint/readmes/PadicHodgeTheoryPartII.md fixes GLX signs, full versus connected groups, coefficient actions and nonnormal-reflex orbit weights. GM0–GM3 prove the forward existence theorem. GM4 consumes it and an independent reverse geometric contract. The Simpson, relative-crystalline and equivariant-curve directions are split in the packet, retaining all assigned routes.

stages.title: Decent fibres and crystalline invariant lines
stages.description: Construct the finite Q_{p^s}-fibre functor from normalized φ^s-eigenspaces, filtration jumps, full-period degree sums and the nonzero Newton–Hodge sets. Classify rank-one coefficient subobjects and prove the full-group invariant-line criterion. Transfer derived containment by the ambient period torsor, keeping full closure H distinct from MT=H°. Imported carriers and period equivalences are not reconstructed.

stages.title: Lowest weights and strict Hodge–Newton estimates
stages.description: Consume the quasisplit generic-filtration supplier and prove the arithmetic degree bound using every distinct Γ_E-orbit and its size weight, including nonnormal reflex fields. Sum through a complete Frobenius period to obtain d_s(v)≤s⟨w_0λ,μ^diamond⟩. The Newton equation gives the opposite lowest-weight bound. Strict positivity of every simple-coroot coefficient forces central highest weights.

stages.title: Generic admissibility and derived monodromy
stages.description: Use the unfiltered decent fibre functor to descend all isocrystal subobjects to one finite coefficient field. Determinantal incidence loci show that a topologically generic flag minimizes their Hodge degrees. Import independent finite-point nonemptiness to prove weak admissibility and apply the parent equivalence. Under strict HN positivity, coefficient lines, the numerical estimates and period comparison yield G_der⊆MT for arbitrary reductive G.

stages.title: Finite-extension period points and central lifting
stages.description: Prove the sparse Witt-coordinate estimate and infinite transcendence of breve Q_p over Q_p. Étale coordinates then give a topologically generic flag over a finite extension containing its reflex field. For every HN-irreducible bounded datum, construct a classical admissible period point with open derived Galois image. Prove equivalence of this existence assertion through a fixed bounded z-extension lift, with the reflex base change and algebraic-monodromy step explicit.

stages.title: Compact torsor stabilizers and the quasisplit converse
stages.description: Identify components of a crystalline G(Q_p)-torsor over Spd K with compact-image cosets, proving compact-orbit connectedness and invariant clopen separation. Obtain open derived stabilizers for reached ambient components, and for all components under an explicit transitivity hypothesis. Finally consume the independent reverse ADLV component/HN implication to deduce HN-irreducibility from MT⊇G_der for quasisplit G. This layer never supplies an input to GM0–GM3.
